transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m having trouble keeping my mind on one thing. Like at work, I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping or some pattern on the screen—or even a siren outside—pulls me off into some other idea before I finish what I was doing.
Are these difficulties with focusing affecting your work performance or daily life in a significant way?
Yeah… it has. Work put me on leave after I pushed some changes without waiting for approval. At home, my wife says the spending and arguing have made things feel kind of unstable.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if it’s fidgety exactly, but I can’t seem to sit with just one thing. I keep jumping into the project—emailing curators, community people, rewriting parts of the backend, sketching out installation ideas, trying to get other developers involved… sometimes late. It just feels bigger than my normal job right now.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah… I guess I do. I spent money we hadn’t really agreed on—GPUs, printing stuff, a promo video. And I pushed an update at work without approval because waiting for another review felt like… like the whole chance was going to disappear.
Do you notice that your impulsive behaviors or restlessness happen when you're feeling particularly happy, excited, or irritable?

Yeah… mostly when I feel really keyed up. Like I’m on, like everything is finally lining up with what I’ve been trying to build here in Glendale. And then if my wife or people at work slow me down with “process” or whatever, I get… pretty irritable. I snap more than I should.
Do you experience these difficulties with focusing and impulsivity at home with your family as much as you do at work?

Yeah… it’s both, I guess. Work is where it got more obvious — they put me on leave after I pushed changes without approval. At home… my wife says the spending and the arguments have made things feel unstable. I don’t really like saying it that way, but… yeah, it’s affecting both.
Do you experience these difficulties with focusing and impulsivity when you're alone as well?

Yeah… even when I’m by myself. I’ll be trying to fix one thing in the code, and then a Slack ping or some color pattern or a siren outside just… pulls me off into some other idea. Then I realize I never finished what I was doing.
Do you think these difficulties with focusing and impulsivity have been present for as long as you can remember?
No… not as long as I can remember. It’s more recent. Maybe about three months, since my platform got picked for the Glendale showcase.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity before the age of 12?
No… not before 12. This is pretty recent — like I said, maybe three months now, since the Glendale showcase thing happened.
Do you find that you have trouble with focusing or impulsivity in quiet, low-stimulation environments?

Yeah… even when it’s quiet, it still happens. I’ll be sitting there trying to fix a rendering bug, and something small—like a Slack ping or just noticing a color pattern—pulls me off into another idea. Then I’ve lost the line I was working on.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or experienced symptoms of another mental health condition, such as depression, anxiety, or bipolar disorder?

I haven’t really thought of it that way. I mean… lately, most days I feel pretty wired—like I’m finally on the right track and people are catching up to what I’ve been building with Glendale. But I do get irritated fast when my wife or people at work slow things down with all their “process” stuff.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy or elevated for most of the day, for several days in a row?

Yeah… I guess so. Most days lately I feel kind of lit up, like I’m unstoppable and Glendale is finally matching what I’ve been building. But if my wife or people at work start slowing me down with “process,” I snap pretty hard.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy or elevated, but not to the point where you lost touch with reality or needed hospitalization?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t think it got to that point. I’ve just felt really lit up most days, like I’m unstoppable and Glendale is finally where I knew it could be. But I do get pretty sharp with people when they slow me down with all the “process” stuff.

Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy or elevated and also experienced at least three other symptoms like increased energy, decreased need for sleep, or excessive talking?

Yeah… I guess increased energy, sure. I’ve been kind of running on this constant current. I wake up already thinking through features, layouts, press angles, code changes… and just sitting still feels like I’m wasting time.
Have you ever been treated for or experienced significant symptoms of a mental health condition other than attention or impulse problems?

Not really treated, no. I mean… I’ve had some things that people might call mental health stuff, I guess. Like I’m pretty sure certain museums and investors have been… watching what I’m building. Some posts and emails line up a little too perfectly to just be random.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy or elevated and also experienced a decreased need for sleep?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep much, but… I don’t know if I needed less sleep or just couldn’t shut my head off.
Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy or elevated and also experienced excessive spending or other impulsive behaviors?

Yeah… there was some of that. I spent money we hadn’t really agreed on—GPUs, print materials, promo videos. And I pushed an update without approval because waiting for another review cycle just felt like… like the whole opportunity was going to die if I didn’t move.
Do you think your feelings of being 'lit up' and unstoppable might be part of a bigger mood issue, rather than just being excited about your project?

Maybe. I don’t know. Most days I do feel… lit up, like things are finally lining up, like Glendale’s catching up to what I’ve been building. And when people slow it down with “process,” my wife or coworkers, I can snap harder than I mean to. So… yeah, maybe it’s bigger than just excitement.
Do you think your feelings of being 'lit up' and unstoppable could be related to a mood issue, such as bipolar disorder, rather than just your project's success?

I guess it could be. I mean, most days I do feel kind of… lit up, like I can just push through anything. Like Glendale finally caught up with what I’ve been building.

But when people slow me down with “process” — my wife, coworkers — I can snap pretty hard. So… maybe it’s not just the project.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy or elevated that lasted for at least four consecutive days?
Yeah… more than four days. It’s been kind of ongoing, I guess—about three months, since my platform got picked for the Glendale showcase.
